messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water freezes at a temperature slightly below the normal 0 °C.  
According to the water phase diagram, the freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly **–2 °C** (about –3.6 °F).  

This is because the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward as pressure decreases, so the melting/freezing temperature drops by about 2 °C per 10 kPa below atmospheric pressure.
